teaching_points: Choose interaction from the evidence the learner must produce; do not reduce a calculation-and-comparison claim to recognition just because selected response is easy to score.
Make every point-bearing requirement visible and accept equivalent units, equations, and rounding that satisfy the stated tolerance.
Use no hint when a useful hint would provide the exact setup being assessed; explain that decision instead of forcing scaffolding.
Treat every name, identifier, option position, count, and value in this example as illustrative; derive fresh values from the current KC and evidence.

kc_groups.name: Comparable nutrition measures
kc_groups.description: Normalize quantities before comparing products with different serving sizes.

leaf_kcs.name: Normalize and compare sodium
leaf_kcs.knowledge_description: To compare sodium when serving sizes differ, convert each label to the same mass basis before choosing the lower value.
leaf_kcs.observable_claim: Given sodium and serving-size values for two foods, the learner can compute both sodium amounts per 100 g and use those results to identify the lower-sodium food.

included: Normalize both label values to 100 g
Show enough work to verify the setup
excluded: Assumptions about ingredients not shown on the labels

source_evidence.supports: Divide the label quantity by serving mass and multiply by 100 before comparing.

assessment_slots.evidence_intent: Compute two normalized sodium values and use them to make the requested comparison.
assessment_slots.justification: The learner must produce and expose two normalization setups, so selected response would not capture the intended evidence. One bounded comparison is sufficient for this worked example.

questions.title: Compare sodium on a common basis

stimulus.text: Food A lists 180 mg sodium per 30 g serving. Food B lists 250 mg sodium per 50 g serving.

questions.prompt: Calculate the sodium per 100 g for both foods, show the two normalization setups, and identify which food is lower in sodium on that basis. Values within 1 mg per 100 g are accepted.

correct_answer.text: Food A: 180 / 30 × 100 = 600 mg per 100 g. Food B: 250 / 50 × 100 = 500 mg per 100 g. Food B is lower on the common 100 g basis. Equivalent correct equations and values within the stated tolerance are accepted.

rubric.criterion: Shows a valid normalization setup for Food A and obtains 600 mg per 100 g within the stated tolerance.
Shows a valid normalization setup for Food B and obtains 500 mg per 100 g within the stated tolerance.
Identifies Food B as lower based on the two normalized values.

questions.answer_explanation: The original serving sizes differ, so the label values become comparable only after both are converted to the same 100 g basis.
questions.hint_absence_reason: The normalization setup is the evidence being assessed, so a procedural hint would supply the central step.
